methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective multicenter (five French centers) cohort analyzing the association between 6-month RECIST 1.1 depth of response and survival in 175 mNSCLC patients. A 6-month landmark partially addresses immortal-time bias, but patients who progressed or died before 6 months were excluded, which is acknowledged and inflates median OS (35 months). Multivariable Cox adjusting for histology, PD-L1, brain metastasis, and metastatic burden was performed (analysis on 139 patients after excluding missing data), with proportional-hazards verification. Thirty-seven percent of patients had different imaging modalities at baseline versus 6 months, which could bias response classification.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort without contemporaneous comparator for the exposure (depth of response is an internal biomarker), mapping to Oxford LoE 4. Results reinforce existing signals that DpR predicts OS in mNSCLC under chemo-ICI, supporting potential early de-escalation strategies but not practice-changing on their own; the findings are hypothesis-generating for prospective de-escalation trials.

reporting_quality.justification: Retrospective observational cohort falling under STROBE; STROBE is not explicitly cited. Inclusion/exclusion, endpoints, and analyses are reported, and limitations (selection bias, imaging-modality heterogeneity, predominance of adenocarcinoma) are openly discussed. Supplementary tables/figures are referenced with redacted URLs; no individual patient data or code availability statement is apparent.

novelty_literature.justification: The prognostic value of depth of response has been repeatedly demonstrated in mNSCLC (Morgenszten 2019, Tachibana 2024) and across tumor types (CLEAR for RCC, melanoma, gastric, pancreatic, colorectal). The SPORE trial adds modest incremental evidence specifically for chemo-ICI combinations with a 6-month landmark, but the conceptual advance is limited and consistent with prior work, which the authors cite extensively.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is concise and clearly organized with adequate tables (demographics, subgroup characteristics, multivariable Cox) and Kaplan-Meier figures. A few typographic and minor issues are present (e.g., overlapping group boundary '0% to -29%' vs '-29% to <0%', 'responss' in Figure 2 legend, swapped Table 3 group 2 range '-30% to -59%') and the abstract duplicates bullet summaries. Discussion is readable but at times meandering around ABCP and cervical cancer detours.

key_strengths: Multicenter French cohort (5 sites, n=175) with mature follow-up (27.7 months median)
Landmark analysis at 6 months with clear HR gradient across 4 response groups (HR 0.31 for -100% to -60%; 2.14 for progression)
Multivariable Cox adjustment for histology, PD-L1, brain metastasis and metastatic burden
Clinically relevant implication for potential de-escalation trials in deep responders
key_concerns: Retrospective design with exclusion of early progressors/deaths inflates survival estimates
37% of patients had different imaging modalities at baseline and 6 months, risking measurement error
Findings largely confirm prior literature (Morgenszten, Tachibana, CLEAR); limited novelty
STROBE not explicitly cited; no data/code sharing statement
Overlapping/typographic inconsistencies in response group definitions (e.g., -29% to 0% vs -29% to <0%)
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid but incremental retrospective cohort confirming the DpR-OS association in chemo-ICI-treated mNSCLC; tier 3 with minor revisions is appropriate given selection bias, imaging heterogeneity, and limited novelty.
